docs.title: Glossary
docs.text: Term Meaning PEFT Parameter-efficient fine-tuning; adapting a model with few trainable parameters. Low rank A compressed matrix representation with rank much smaller than the full dimension. LoRA Low-Rank Adaptation, a PEFT method that trains low-rank weight updates. Soft prompt A learned continuous prompt embedding rather than manually written text. Adapter A small trainable module inserted into a pretrained network. IA3 A lightweight method using learned multiplicative vectors inside transformer computations.

docs.title: Big Picture
docs.text:
Training with human feedback addresses the gap between next-token prediction and the user-facing objective of producing responses that are helpful, honest, and harmless. Instruction tuning teaches a model to follow instructions, but human preference training is used when correctness alone is not enough to capture tone, usefulness, safety, and social expectations.

The lecture presents two preference-learning routes: reinforcement learning from human feedback, which trains an explicit reward model and then optimises a policy with PPO, and direct preference optimisation, which learns directly from chosen/rejected responses without a separate reward model or reinforcement-learning loop.

docs.title: Learning Map
docs.text:
• Prerequisite ideas: instruction tuning, supervised fine-tuning, language-model probabilities, reinforcement learning, and transformer hidden states.
  • Core concepts: helpful-honest-harmless alignment, SFT, preference pairs, reward models, Bradley-Terry probability, PPO, KL penalty, PPO-ptx, and DPO.
  • Main procedures: collect demonstrations, train an SFT model, collect ranked responses, train a reward model, update the policy with PPO, or bypass the reward model with DPO.
  • Tutorial skills: explain why a reward model is not enough to update an LM, compute the intuition of clipped PPO updates, and diagnose reward-model overfitting to superficial preference cues.
  • Common traps: assuming human feedback represents universal human values, treating PPO clipping as always using only the clipped term, or forgetting that reward models can be gamed.

docs.title: Alignment problem
docs.text:
Large LMs can produce technically correct text that is blunt, unhelpful, unsafe, or socially misaligned. The lecture frames preference learning as teaching the model how humans want to communicate, not just how to predict likely text.

The three target qualities are helpfulness, honesty, and harmlessness: the model should solve the user's task, avoid unsupported certainty or falsehood, and avoid causing harm.

docs.title: Supervised fine-tuning
docs.text:
The first RLHF stage collects prompts and ideal answers, then fine-tunes a pretrained model on those demonstrations. In the InstructGPT pipeline, the lecture describes high-quality data collection by humans, including experts and crowdworkers, followed by supervised fine-tuning.

SFT is instruction tuning in this pipeline: it teaches the model to imitate desired answers, but it does not by itself optimise nuanced human preference trade-offs.

docs.title: Reward model
docs.text:
The reward-model stage samples several outputs from the SFT model for the same prompt, asks human labelers to rank or compare those outputs, and trains a model that maps a prompt-response pair to a scalar reward.

Pairwise preference data can be represented as a context, a chosen response, and a rejected response. The reward model is trained so the chosen response receives a higher score than the rejected response.

The lecture uses the Bradley-Terry formulation to turn two reward scores into the probability that the chosen response is preferred. Lower loss means the reward model is more aligned with the observed human preference pair.

docs.title: PPO policy optimisation
docs.text:
A reward model scores outputs but does not tell the language model exactly how to change token probabilities. PPO supplies a constrained policy-optimisation step that updates the SFT model toward higher-reward outputs.

PPO uses a probability ratio between the current and old policy and an advantage estimate based on reward relative to a baseline. Clipping prevents overly large updates, so the policy is nudged in the preferred direction without changing too much in one step.

The unclipped objective remains necessary because the minimum of clipped and unclipped terms depends on the sign and scale of the advantage; using only the clipped term would not correctly represent all update cases.

docs.title: KL penalty and PPO-ptx
docs.text:
The lecture adds a per-token KL penalty from the frozen SFT model to reduce reward-model overoptimisation. This keeps the updated model close to a trusted baseline distribution instead of drifting into unnatural text that exploits the reward model.

PPO-ptx adds a pretraining loss during PPO to mitigate performance regressions on public NLP datasets.

docs.title: Direct preference optimisation
docs.text:
Direct preference optimisation removes the explicit reward model and reinforcement-learning stage. Instead, it uses model log-probabilities for preferred and rejected completions and applies a contrastive preference loss so the policy directly assigns higher probability to preferred outputs.

DPO is presented as lower-complexity than RLHF because it avoids training separate SFT, reward, and policy components through multiple stages.

docs.title: RLHF pipeline
docs.text:
1. Collect prompts.
  2. Collect human-written ideal answers.
  3. Train an SFT model.
  4. Sample multiple outputs from the SFT model.
  5. Collect human rankings or pairwise preferences.
  6. Train a reward model on chosen/rejected responses.
  7. Optimise the language-model policy with PPO using reward scores and constraints such as KL penalties.

docs.title: DPO pipeline
docs.text:
1. Collect preference pairs for the same prompt.
  2. Use the model's log-probabilities for the chosen and rejected responses.
  3. Optimise a contrastive preference loss that increases preference for chosen responses.
  4. Avoid a separately learned reward model and PPO loop.

docs.title: Big Picture
docs.text:
Multimodal large language models extend LLM-style instruction following beyond text so the model can process, understand, and sometimes generate across modalities such as image, video, audio, sensors, and text. The core motivation is that humans combine multiple senses, and single-modality language loses context that may be crucial for interpretation.

The lecture frames MLLMs as an extension of prompting, instruction tuning, PEFT, and human-feedback training into multimodal settings. The key engineering problem is how to connect modality-specific encoders and generators to an LLM backbone while preserving alignment, efficiency, and cross-modal consistency.

docs.title: Learning Map
docs.text:
• Prerequisite ideas: LLMs, instruction tuning, PEFT, transformer encoders, visual encoders, and evaluation benchmarks.
  • Core concepts: modality, MLLM architecture, input projector, output projector, visual/audio encoders, cross-modal alignment, LVLM instruction tuning, multimodal chain-of-thought, and multimodal distillation.
  • Main procedures: build modality-specific representations, project them into the LLM space, tune selected bridge modules or adapters, and evaluate on multimodal tasks and benchmarks.
  • Common traps: treating multimodality as only image captioning, ignoring annotation and privacy costs, or assuming frozen backbones can adapt to every new modality without workarounds.

docs.title: Multimodality
docs.text:
[!definition] Multimodality is the ability of a model to process, understand, and generate data from multiple sources such as text, images, audio, video, and sensors.

Multimodality improves contextual understanding because different modalities carry complementary evidence. For example, sarcasm, actions, medical conditions, or driving scenes may need visual, audio, sensor, and textual evidence together.

docs.title: Datasets and benchmarks
docs.text:
MLLM tasks include general vision-language tasks such as visual question answering, image captioning, visual reasoning, image-text retrieval, report generation, referring expression tasks, segmentation, and domain-specific tasks in geography, medicine, robotics, autonomous driving, and visually rich documents.

Pretraining data can be coarse-grained image-text data from the web, fine-grained image-text descriptions, video-text datasets, or audio-text datasets. Coarse web data is large but noisy; fine-grained descriptions can be higher quality but require stronger generation or annotation pipelines.

Dataset creation is difficult because multimodal data collection requires diverse sources and tools, annotation is costly and specialised, labels can be ambiguous, and cross-modal synchronisation must align text, video, audio, or sensor streams.

docs.title: MLLM architecture
docs.text:
A typical MLLM uses modality-specific encoders, an input projector, an LLM backbone, and optionally output projectors or modality generators. Visual encoders can include ViT/OpenCLIP/DINO-style models, while audio encoders can include HuBERT/BEATs/Whisper/CLAP-style models.

Input projectors map non-text modality features into a representation the LLM can use. Output projectors or generators let the model generate modalities such as image, video, or audio.

Architecture challenges include dependency on frozen pretrained backbones, high computation from separate encoders and projectors, limited flexibility for new modalities, and inconsistent multimodal evaluation.

docs.title: Visual instruction tuning
docs.text:
Visual instruction tuning trains a vision-language model to follow image-grounded instructions. LLaVA connects a vision encoder with a language model and instruction-tunes on generated vision-language instruction data.

LLaVA-1.5 shows that strong baselines can come from simple design choices: an MLP connector, CLIP-ViT-L-336px, and academic VQA data with response-formatting prompts.

docs.title: Multimodal chain-of-thought
docs.text: Multimodal chain-of-thought introduces reasoning or rationale generation into MLLMs, extending the chain-of-thought idea from text-only prompting to multimodal reasoning.

docs.title: Multimodal knowledge distillation
docs.text: Knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from a large teacher model to a smaller student model. In multimodal systems, distillation can involve output distributions, intermediate features, attention maps, and multiple teachers for different modalities.

docs.title: Building an MLLM
docs.text:
1. Choose the target modalities and tasks.
  2. Select modality encoders for image, video, audio, sensors, or other inputs.
  3. Use an input projector to align modality features with the LLM backbone.
  4. Tune bridge modules, projection layers, adapters, or prompts.
  5. Evaluate task performance and cross-modal consistency.

docs.title: LVLM instruction tuning
docs.text:
1. Build a corpus of image-instruction-target examples.
  2. Freeze core vision and language foundation models where appropriate.
  3. Fine-tune bridge modules or projection layers.
  4. Use diverse instruction templates for captioning, VQA, visual reasoning, and other tasks.

docs.title: Big Picture
docs.text:
Retrieval-augmented language models use external datastores or knowledge bases so generation is not limited to static parametric knowledge. The model can look up supporting documents or facts during inference and use them as context before producing an answer.

Knowledge-augmented LMs extend this idea from unstructured retrieved text to structured knowledge such as knowledge graphs and commonsense resources. This is important because relevant facts are not always useful reasoning paths, and parametric knowledge can be stale, opaque, or difficult to verify.

docs.title: Learning Map
docs.text:
• Prerequisite ideas: LLM prompting, vector similarity, indexing, transformers, knowledge graphs, and chain-of-thought prompting.
  • Core concepts: datastore, retriever, top-k documents, RAG, frozen RAG, RETRO, sparse retrieval, dense retrieval, knowledge graph, KG-CoT, ConceptNet, and ATOMIC.
  • Main procedures: retrieve relevant context, add it to the prompt or architecture, generate with evidence, or construct KG reasoning paths for the LLM.
  • Common traps: assuming all retrieved text is reliable, confusing retrieval relevance with reasoning usefulness, or ignoring indexing cost during training.

docs.title: Retrieval-augmented language model
docs.text:
[!definition] A retrieval-augmented LM retrieves relevant information from an external datastore or knowledge base and conditions generation on that information.

RAG can be summarised as retrieve, add, generate: retrieve relevant information, add it to the user prompt or model context, then generate an answer using the augmented context.

Retrieval improves interpretability and control because retrieved sources can be traced and cited, but it also introduces retrieval quality, relevance, and datastore governance problems.

docs.title: Two RALM paths
docs.text:
One path builds a language model with a built-in retrieval component, as in RETRO. This treats retrieval as part of the architecture and raises technical questions about datastore granularity, retriever representation, and how retrieved contexts are integrated into transformer layers.

The second path treats retrieval as a tool used by an already powerful frozen LLM. In this pattern, a retrieval API or search engine is called when needed and returned results are inserted into context.

docs.title: RETRO
docs.text:
RETRO retrieves chunks of 64 tokens using frozen BERT representations and integrates retrieved contexts through extra encoder/cross-attention machinery inside a transformer.

The lecture highlights that RETRO uses 150M to 7B parameter LMs with a datastore up to about 2T tokens and can obtain comparable performance to GPT-3 on the Pile with far fewer parameters, although it is not a specialised QA model.

Training retrieval-augmented models is hard because both the LM and retriever/index may be large, and updating an index during training is expensive.

docs.title: Knowledge graphs
docs.text:
A knowledge graph is a directed labelled graph where entities are nodes and relationships are labelled edges. Knowledge graphs can integrate structured, semi-structured, and unstructured sources into a connected representation.

Domain-specific knowledge graphs can be used in clinical, financial, and legal settings where specialist knowledge matters.

docs.title: KG-CoT
docs.text:
KG-CoT uses a small graph reasoning model to build explicit reasoning paths over a knowledge graph, then provides those paths to a large LLM for knowledge-aware question answering.

KG-CoT addresses two problems: LLM parametric knowledge may be unavailable, outdated, or unreliable, and fragmented retrieved facts may be relevant without forming a coherent reasoning path.

docs.title: Commonsense knowledge
docs.text: Commonsense resources such as ConceptNet and ATOMIC encode everyday semantic or event knowledge that can augment LMs in tasks requiring implicit world knowledge.

docs.title: RAG workflow
docs.text:
1. Store documents, chunks, or facts in a datastore.
  2. Represent the query and datastore items for retrieval.
  3. Search for top-k relevant items using sparse or dense retrieval.
  4. Add retrieved context to the prompt or integrate it inside the architecture.
  5. Generate the answer and preserve evidence traceability where possible.

docs.title: KG reasoning workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify entities or concepts in the question.
  2. Retrieve or traverse relevant graph relations.
  3. Build explicit reasoning paths rather than isolated facts.
  4. Provide the paths as knowledge chains to the LLM.
  5. Generate a knowledge-aware answer.

docs.title: Big Picture
docs.text:
Ethics in NLP is about the relationship between language technologies, people, and social consequences. Legal permission is not enough: public data, model predictions, and deployment choices can still violate consent, social expectations, privacy, fairness, or safety.

The lecture uses bias, misclassification, public data, word embeddings, and text-to-image generation to show that NLP systems can reproduce and amplify social stereotypes. Ethical analysis therefore needs to ask who benefits, who is harmed, who consented, and who is responsible.

docs.title: Learning Map
docs.text:
• Prerequisite ideas: classification, embeddings, LLMs, training data, evaluation, and deployment.
  • Core concepts: law vs ethics, consent, public vs publicised data, social contract, representativeness, stereotypes, bias amplification, misclassification cost, and ethical responsibility.
  • Main procedures: identify stakeholders, benefits, harms, consent issues, dataset gaps, misuse risks, and responsibility.
  • Common traps: equating legal with ethical, ignoring social context, or evaluating only average accuracy when misclassification harms are uneven.

docs.title: Law vs ethics
docs.text:
Laws are written rules with formal punishment; ethics are guiding moral principles and values that can be unwritten, socially enforced, and context-dependent.

Ethical questions often have grey areas and can change with social values over time. A system can be legal while still being ethically problematic.

docs.title: Language technologies and people
docs.text:
Language is not only about words and meanings; NLP systems affect people and societies through data collection, modelling, deployment, and interpretation decisions.

Ethical review should connect technical choices to real-world consequences, especially when models are used for sensitive classifications or social decisions.

docs.title: Consent and public data
docs.text:
Using online data can be legal but still ethically problematic if people did not consent to the specific use. Public availability does not imply that data was intended to be publicised, analysed, or used for sensitive inference.

Dataset representativeness matters because gaps in population coverage can produce biased or misleading model behaviour.

docs.title: Bias in embeddings and generation
docs.text:
Word embeddings can reflect and amplify gender stereotypes, as analogy structure may encode associations such as men with programmers and women with housekeepers, or fathers with doctors and mothers with nurses.

Text-to-image generation can also express bias because image outputs depend on stereotypes and distributions learned from training data.

docs.title: Misclassification cost
docs.text: Misclassification costs depend on social context. A model can have good aggregate performance while still causing serious harm to particular groups or individuals.

docs.title: Ethical risk checklist
docs.text:
1. Identify who benefits from the system.
  2. Identify who can be harmed and how.
  3. Check consent and intended use of data.
  4. Check whether the dataset is representative.
  5. Identify misuse risks.
  6. Identify who is responsible across researchers, developers, managers, institutions, and society.

docs.title: Bias analysis workflow
docs.text:
1. Inspect the data source and label distribution.
  2. Look for social stereotypes in text, embeddings, or generated outputs.
  3. Evaluate performance and harms across groups.
  4. Consider whether the task should be built at all.
  5. Document ethical considerations and mitigation limits.

docs.title: Tutorial Patterns
docs.text: Pattern What to Recognize How to Solve Common Mistake Public dataset scenario data is visible online but sensitive ask about consent, publicised use, social contract, and representativeness saying legal access is sufficient Sensitive classifier predicts traits from photos/text identify beneficiaries, harms, misuse, and responsibility evaluating only predictive accuracy Embedding bias analogy reveals stereotype explain learned social association and amplification treating vector arithmetic as neutral truth Misclassification cost errors affect groups unevenly evaluate harm in social context assuming all false positives/negatives are equal

docs.text: Concept Meaning Course implication Legal permitted by rules necessary but not sufficient Ethical consistent with values, consent, and social responsibility requires stakeholder and harm analysis Public accessible to others does not imply consent for all uses Publicised actively exposed or amplified can violate expectations even if source was public

docs.title: Big Picture
docs.text:
The subject review consolidates the full semester into exam-ready themes: preprocessing, n-gram language models, classification, POS tagging and HMMs, feedforward networks, recurrent networks, transformers, word embeddings, pretrained models, LLMs, prompting, PEFT, RLHF, multimodal LLMs, retrieval and knowledge augmentation, and ethics.

The exam is closed book, on campus, allows a non-programmable calculator, has 120 points, and has 120 minutes writing time plus 15 minutes reading time. It contains short answer, method, and algorithm questions.

docs.title: 18 Guest Lecture: AI Intro for Nontechnical Audiences
Big Picture
docs.text:
The guest lecture introduces AI and LLMs for a nontechnical audience. It connects basic machine learning, neural networks, language modelling, generative LLM behaviour, limitations, deployment options, robotics, autonomous driving, world models, emotion, and long-term social impacts.

Its main practical message is that generative AI is useful for some tasks and weak for others; it is not "taking over", but it is becoming embedded in work, productivity, robotics, and decision systems.

docs.title: Learning Map
docs.text:
• Prerequisite ideas: data examples, features, classification, neural network weights, and language-model next-token prediction.
  • Core concepts: machine learning today, neural-network structure, LLM generation, limitations, AI deployment models, world models, emotion prompting, and social disruption.
  • Main procedures: encode data as vectors, build a neural network, train on input-output examples, and use the trained system on new vectors.
  • Common traps: treating LLM outputs as truth, assuming LLMs reason logically, assuming models have goals, or assuming AI impact is uniformly immediate.

docs.title: Machine learning workflow
docs.text:
Machine learning uses examples and features to learn patterns that can be applied to new cases. The guest lecture illustrates this with tabular classification and the iris dataset.

Neural-network construction involves encoding data as numerical vectors, choosing nodes, layers, connections, node functions, outputs, and then training weights using many input-output examples.

docs.title: Neural language models
docs.text:
A language model is described as a learned list of word-sequence continuations. A neural network language model learns these continuations through a powerful parameterised system rather than a hand-written list.

Generative LLMs generate left to right by repeatedly selecting continuations conditioned on the previous context.

docs.title: LLM limitations
docs.text:
The guest lecture emphasises that an LLM has no direct understanding of truth, can combine true fragments into false statements, cannot perform reliable logical checking by default, and has no goals or wishes.

The practical conclusion is to use one's own judgement rather than outsourcing truth and reasoning to generated text.

docs.title: AI deployment options
docs.text: Deployment choices range from buying packaged tools, contracting with major providers, running private cloud systems with RAG, using smaller vendors, or running open models on premises. More privacy and control generally require more cost and expertise.

docs.title: Future directions
docs.text:
The lecture identifies three major NLP directions: engineering work to make LLMs usable, application work to make LLMs useful, and research work to make LLMs understandable or at least reliable engineering systems.

Long-term advantage is framed around human factors such as creativity, relationships, business design, distribution, partnerships, and customer experiences built around AI.

docs.title: Neural-network construction
docs.text:
1. Encode data as numerical vectors.
  2. Choose network structure, nodes, layers, links, node functions, and outputs.
  3. Train the network on input-output examples to adjust weights.
  4. Use the trained network on new inputs.

docs.title: Practical LLM use
docs.text:
1. Use LLMs for tasks where generation, summarisation, drafting, or pattern matching is useful.
  2. Check factual claims and reasoning.
  3. Consider privacy, cost, and deployment model.
  4. Treat output as assistance, not authority.

闭卷复习顺序建议：

  1. 先背本页的 keyword index 和 master checklist，确保知道每个主题会问什么。
  2. 再逐主题复习详细 sections，重点练公式、例子和 traps。
  3. 对每个 topic 自测三句话：What is it? Why use it? When does it fail?
  4. 数学题必须写中间步骤；概念题必须给 contrast；伦理题必须给 stakeholder 和 harm。

docs.title: 0.4 Highest-Priority Exam Traps
docs.text:
• Do not omit </s> in sentence probability.
  • Do not divide n-gram MLE by total corpus size when conditioning on a context.
  • Do not call interpolation “backoff”; interpolation always mixes models.
  • Do not run POS tagging greedily when the question asks for HMM/Viterbi.
  • Do not say attention weights are applied to keys; they are applied to values.
  • Do not say BERT is decoder-only or GPT is bidirectional.
  • Do not treat instruction tuning, SFT, RLHF and DPO as the same operation.
  • Do not say Reward Model generates answers; the policy model generates answers.
  • Do not say DPO does not update model weights; it updates policy without explicit RM/PPO.
  • Do not equate public data with ethical consent.

docs.title: 1. MaxMatch
docs.text:
MaxMatch（最大匹配）假设已有词表，从当前位置贪心选择词表中能够匹配的最长词。

V = {墨, 大, 的, 学, 生, 与, 众, 不, 同, 墨大, 学生, 不同, 与众不同}

墨大的学生与众不同
墨大 | 的学生与众不同
墨大 | 的 | 学生与众不同
墨大 | 的 | 学生 | 与众不同

结果：墨大 / 的 / 学生 / 与众不同。

局限：依赖固定 vocabulary；最长匹配不保证语义正确。例如 去买新西兰花 可以表示 去 / 买 / 新西兰 / 花，也可以表示 去 / 买 / 新 / 西兰花。

[!note]- MaxMatch 例子：墨大的学生与众不同

  • 当前字符串以 墨大 开头；词表同时包含 墨 和 墨大，因此选择更长的 墨大
  • 剩余字符串依次选择 的、学生、与众不同
  • 最终结果：墨大 / 的 / 学生 / 与众不同
  • 反例 去买新西兰花 表明 longest match 不一定等于 intended meaning

docs.title: 2. Byte-Pair Encoding
docs.text:
BPE（Byte-Pair Encoding）从字符开始，反复合并语料中频率最高的相邻符号对：

  1. 将训练词拆成字符。
  2. 统计所有相邻 pair。
  3. 合并频率最高的 pair。
  4. 重新统计并继续合并，直到达到 merge budget 或目标词表大小。

Claim: merge 依据 corpus frequency，而非 semantic similarity。高频词可能成为单独 token，罕见词和 unseen word 仍可由 subword 组成。

[!note]- BPE 例子：从 character 到 subword

  • 讲义将 Colourless green ideas sleep furiously 表示为 [colour] [less] [green] [idea] [s] [sleep] [furious] [ly]
  • 初始 vocabulary 只包含 characters
  • 每轮合并 corpus 中 frequency 最高的 adjacent pair，例如频繁出现的字符序列逐步形成 colour 或 furious
  • Common word 可能成为完整 token；rare/unseen word 仍可由较小 subwords 表示

docs.title: Chain rule 与 Markov assumption
docs.text:
\[ P(w_{1:m})=\prod_{i=1}^{m}P(w_i\mid w_{1:i-1}) \] \[ P(w_i\mid w_{1:i-1}) \approx P(w_i\mid w_{i-n+1:i-1}) \]
  • unigram：不看前文；bigram：看前 1 个词；trigram：看前 2 个词。
  • <s>、</s> 表示句子开始和结束；计算句子概率时不要漏掉 </s>。

[!note]- Trigram 例子：yes no no yes

  • 使用两个 start symbols：<s> <s> yes no no yes </s>
  • \(P(\text{yes}\mid<s>,<s>)\) 预测第一个词
  • \(P(\text{no}\mid<s>,\text{yes})\)、\(P(\text{no}\mid\text{yes},\text{no})\) 等项只看前两个 tokens
  • 最后必须乘 \(P(</s>\mid\text{no},\text{yes})\)，因为 sentence ending 也需要预测

docs.title: Maximum-Likelihood Estimation
docs.text:
\[ P_{\mathrm{MLE}}(w_i\mid h) = \frac{C(h,w_i)}{C(h)} \]

其中 \(h\) 是前面的 context。Bigram 例：

\[ P(\text{chuck}\mid\text{wood}) = \frac{C(\text{wood chuck})}{C(\text{wood})} \]

易错点：条件概率的分母是 context count，不是总 token 数。任何 unseen n-gram 都会得到 0，并使整个序列概率变成 0，因此需要 smoothing。

[!note]- N-gram MLE 例子：wood chuck

  • Workshop corpus 中 \(C(\text{wood})=8\)，\(C(\text{wood chuck})=4\)
  • \(P(\text{chuck}\mid\text{wood})=4/8=1/2\)
  • 若 \(C(\text{wood could})=0\)，则 \(P(\text{could}\mid\text{wood})=0\)
  • 一个 conditional probability 为 0，就会让整句概率的乘积变成 0

docs.title: Add-one / Laplacian
docs.text:
假装每个可能的 n-gram 都额外出现一次：

\[ P_{\text{add-1}}(w_i\mid h) = \frac{C(h,w_i)+1}{C(h)+|V|} \]

讲义例子：<s> the rat ate the cheese </s>，\(|V|=5\)。

\[ P(\text{ate}\mid\text{rat})=\frac{1+1}{1+5}=\frac{2}{6} \] \[ P(\text{ate}\mid\text{cheese})=\frac{0+1}{1+5}=\frac{1}{6} \]

<s> 不属于 vocabulary，因为模型不需要预测它；</s> 属于 vocabulary，因为模型需要预测句子结束。

[!note]- Add-one 例子：the rat ate the cheese

  • \(V=\{\text{the, rat, ate, cheese, }</s>\}\)，所以 \(|V|=5\)
  • Seen bigram：\(P(\text{ate}\mid\text{rat})=(1+1)/(1+5)=2/6\)
  • Unseen bigram：\(P(\text{ate}\mid\text{cheese})=(0+1)/(1+5)=1/6\)
  • Unseen event 因此获得 non-zero probability

docs.title: Add-k / Lidstone / Add-alpha
docs.text:
Add-one 往往分配过多概率给 unseen events，因此改为加入较小的 \(k\)：

\[ P_{\text{add-}k}(w_i\mid h) = \frac{C(h,w_i)+k}{C(h)+k|V|} \]
  • \(k=1\) 时退化为 add-one。
  • \(0<k<1\) 通常比 add-one 温和，但需要选择 \(k\)。

[!note]- Add-k 例子：context alleged

  • 教材示例中 alleged 后共有 5 个 observed bigrams、2 个 unobserved bigrams，\(C(\text{alleged})=20\)
  • 取 \(k=0.1\)、\(|V|=7\) 时，seen count 为 8 的 continuation 得到 \((8+0.1)/(20+7\times0.1)\)
  • Unseen continuation 得到 \((0+0.1)/(20+7\times0.1)\)
  • 与 add-one 相比，较小的 \(k\) 不会把过多 mass 转移给 unseen events

docs.title: Absolute Discounting
docs.text:
从每个 observed n-gram 的计数中减去固定 discount \(D\)，将留下的 probability mass 分给 unseen n-grams：

\[ P_{\mathrm{AD}}(w_i\mid h) = \frac{C(h,w_i)-D}{C(h)} \qquad\text{if }C(h,w_i)>0 \]

若 context \(h\) 后有 \(N_{1+}(h,*)\) 个 observed continuation，则释放的总概率质量为：

\[ \frac{D\,N_{1+}(h,*)}{C(h)} \]

教材中的基础 absolute discounting 将这部分质量平均分给 unseen n-grams。

[!example]- Absolute Discounting 清晰例子：context eat

假设 vocabulary 中，eat 后可能出现 5 个词：

Bigram Original count eat apples 5 eat rice 3 eat bread 2 eat soup 0 eat salad 0

因此 \(C(\text{eat})=10\)。不使用 smoothing 时，soup 和 salad 的概率都是 0。

令固定 discount \(D=0.5\)。只对 3 个 observed bigrams 减去 \(0.5\)：

Bigram Discounted count Probability eat apples \(5-0.5=4.5\) \(4.5/10=0.45\) eat rice \(3-0.5=2.5\) \(2.5/10=0.25\) eat bread \(2-0.5=1.5\) \(1.5/10=0.15\)

释放的 probability mass 为：

\[ \frac{D\,N_{1+}(\text{eat},*)}{C(\text{eat})} = \frac{0.5\times3}{10} = 0.15 \]

基础版本将 \(0.15\) 平均分给 2 个 unseen continuations：

\[ P(\text{soup}\mid\text{eat}) = P(\text{salad}\mid\text{eat}) = \frac{0.15}{2} = 0.075 \]

最后验证归一化：\(0.45+0.25+0.15+0.075+0.075=1\)。

记忆方式：每个 seen event 都“让出”固定 count \(D\)；让出的总 mass 再交给 unseen events。

[!note]- Absolute Discounting 例子：context alleged

  • 教材示例有 5 个 observed continuations、2 个 unseen continuations，context count 为 20
  • 若 \(D=0.1\)，每个 seen count 都减去 \(0.1\)
  • 释放的 mass 为 \((0.1\times5)/20\)
  • 基础版本将该 mass 平均分给 2 个 unseen continuations

docs.title: Katz Backoff
docs.text:
高阶 n-gram 已见过时使用 discounted probability；未见过时按 lower-order model 分配剩余质量：

\[ P_{\mathrm{Katz}}(w_i\mid h)= \begin{cases} \dfrac{C(h,w_i)-D}{C(h)}, & C(h,w_i)>0\\[6pt] \alpha(h)P_{\mathrm{lower}}(w_i), & C(h,w_i)=0 \end{cases} \]

\(\alpha(h)\) 负责归一化，使所有概率之和为 1。

局限：lower-order raw frequency 未必代表合理 continuation。对 reading ___，若 Francisco 的 unigram frequency 高于 glasses，Katz backoff 可能错误偏向 Francisco。

[!note]- Katz Backoff 例子：reading ___

  • \(C(\text{reading glasses})=C(\text{reading Francisco})=0\)，两个 bigrams 都 unseen
  • 模型因此 back off 到 lower-order unigram probabilities
  • 若 \(C(\text{Francisco})>C(\text{glasses})\)，Katz backoff 会给 Francisco 更高概率
  • 但 reading glasses 明显更合理，说明 raw frequency 不等于 continuation suitability

docs.title: Kneser-Ney
docs.text:
Kneser-Ney 不只看词本身多常见，而看它能出现在多少种不同 context 后，即 continuation probability：

\[ P_{\mathrm{cont}}(w) \propto N_{1+}(*,w) = \left|\{u:C(u,w)>0\}\right| \]

Bigram 形式：

\[ P_{\mathrm{KN}}(w_i\mid w_{i-1})= \begin{cases} \dfrac{C(w_{i-1},w_i)-D}{C(w_{i-1})}, & C(w_{i-1},w_i)>0\\[6pt] \beta(w_{i-1})P_{\mathrm{cont}}(w_i), & C(w_{i-1},w_i)=0 \end{cases} \]

glasses 可接在许多不同词后，continuation count 高；Francisco 主要接在 San 后，continuation count 低。Workshop 例子中：

chuck <- {wood, chuck, would, could}  => 4
wood  <- {much, a, chuck, the}       => 4
Pcont(chuck) = Pcont(wood) = 4/18

Claim: Kneser-Ney rewards contextual versatility，而不是 raw frequency。

[!note]- Kneser-Ney 例子：glasses 与 Francisco

  • glasses 可出现在 reading glasses、black glasses、buy glasses 等许多 contexts 中
  • Francisco 很常见，但主要出现在 San Francisco 这一种 context 中
  • 因此 glasses 的 continuation count 更高，适合在 unseen context 中获得更高概率
  • Workshop 中 chuck 和 wood 各有 4 个 unique preceding words，所以两者的 \(P_{\mathrm{cont}}\) 都是 \(4/18\)

docs.title: Interpolation
docs.text:
始终以权重混合不同阶数的 n-gram model。Interpolated trigram：

\[ P_{\mathrm{IN}}(w_i\mid w_{i-2},w_{i-1}) = \lambda_3P_3(w_i\mid w_{i-2},w_{i-1}) +\lambda_2P_2(w_i\mid w_{i-1}) +\lambda_1P_1(w_i) \] \[ \lambda_1+\lambda_2+\lambda_3=1 \]

\(\lambda\) 通常基于 held-out data 学习。

[!note]- Interpolation 例子：预测 trigram 中的下一个词

  • 即使 trigram \(P_3(w_i\mid w_{i-2},w_{i-1})\) 已经 observed，模型仍同时使用 bigram 和 unigram
  • 例如取 \(\lambda_3=0.6\)、\(\lambda_2=0.3\)、\(\lambda_1=0.1\)
  • 最终概率为 \(0.6P_3+0.3P_2+0.1P_1\)
  • 与 backoff 不同，interpolation 并非只在 higher-order n-gram unseen 时才使用 lower-order model

docs.title: 5. Smoothing 对比
docs.text: 方法 如何处理 unseen n-gram Lower-order information 关键点 Add-one 所有 count 加 1 否 简单，但通常 smoothing 过强 Add-k 所有 count 加 \(k\) 否 比 add-one 温和，需要选 \(k\) Absolute discounting 从 seen count 减 \(D\)，质量给 unseen 否 基础版本平均分配剩余质量 Katz backoff unseen 时回退 仅在需要时 raw lower-order frequency 可能误导 Kneser-Ney unseen 时使用 continuation probability 是 奖励出现在多种 context 中的词 Interpolation 加权混合所有阶数 始终使用 不是只在 unseen 时才回退

docs.title: Exam Traps
docs.text:
• 漏掉 sentence-end probability \(P(</s>\mid h)\)。
  • MLE 条件概率错误地除以总 token 数，而不是 \(C(h)\)。
  • Add-one/Add-k 只修改 numerator，忘记修改 denominator。
  • 把 backoff 当成始终混合多个模型；始终混合是 interpolation。
  • 把 Kneser-Ney continuation count 当成 raw word frequency。
  • 忽略 larger \(n\) 带来更强 local context，同时也带来更严重 sparsity。

docs.title: Core Task
docs.text:
Text classification：给一段文本分配一个 label。 输入可以是 document、sentence、review、email 或 tweet；输出是固定 label set 中的一个或多个类别。

"This movie was painfully slow."  -> negative
"Win a free prize now!"           -> spam
"The policy rate increased."      -> finance/news category

常见流程：

Raw text
  -> preprocessing/tokenisation
  -> feature representation
  -> train classifier
  -> evaluate on held-out data
  -> inspect errors

Claim: Text classification performance depends on both the model and the representation of text as features.

docs.title: Data Splits and Evaluation Setup
docs.text:
Split Role Exam wording to use Training set fit model parameters model learns weights/probabilities from this data Development/validation set tune hyperparameters, choose features do not report final performance on dev after repeated tuning Test set final unbiased estimate touched once after model selection

Do not evaluate on training data only; high training accuracy can be overfitting.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Representation Description Strength Weakness Bag-of-Words count or binary presence of words simple and strong baseline loses word order TF-IDF downweights corpus-wide common words useful for document classification sparse and high-dimensional n-gram features word/character sequences captures phrases like not good larger feature space hand-built features length, punctuation, lexicons, metadata injects task knowledge brittle/domain-specific embeddings dense vectors from pretrained models semantic sharing may hide errors/bias

Example: sentiment classification should treat good and not good differently, so bigram features can help.

docs.title: Naive Bayes
docs.text:
Naive Bayes applies Bayes' rule with a conditional independence assumption over features:

\[ \hat c =\arg\max_c P(c)\prod_i P(f_i\mid c) \]

For text, \(f_i\) can be words. In log space:

\[ \hat c =\arg\max_c \left[ \log P(c)+\sum_i\log P(w_i\mid c) \right] \]

MLE with add-k smoothing:

\[ P(w\mid c)= \frac{C(w,c)+k} {\sum_{w'}C(w',c)+k|V|} \]

Minimum worked example:

Class spam has high counts for "free", "win", "prize".
Class ham has high counts for "meeting", "project".
Email: "free prize"
NB compares P(spam)P(free|spam)P(prize|spam)
        vs P(ham)P(free|ham)P(prize|ham).

Trap: the independence assumption is not literally true; it is a modelling approximation that often works well for sparse text features.

docs.title: Logistic Regression
docs.text:
Binary logistic regression:

\[ P(y=1\mid x)=\sigma(w^\top x+b) =\frac{1}{1+\exp(-(w^\top x+b))} \]

Multiclass softmax:

\[ P(y=c\mid x) = \frac{\exp(w_c^\top x+b_c)} {\sum_{c'}\exp(w_{c'}^\top x+b_{c'})} \]

Training minimises negative log-likelihood / cross-entropy, often with regularisation:

\[ \mathcal L =-\sum_n\log P(y^{(n)}\mid x^{(n)}) +\lambda\|w\|_2^2 \]

Interpretation:

  • positive weight on excellent for positive sentiment increases \(P(\text{positive})\);
  • negative weight on boring decreases it;
  • regularisation reduces overfitting by discouraging very large weights.

docs.title: SVM and kNN
docs.text:
Method Core idea Good when Weakness SVM find a separating hyperplane with large margin high-dimensional sparse text less probabilistic; kernel/parameter choices matter kNN classify by nearest labelled examples local similarity is meaningful slow at prediction; sensitive to distance metric and feature scaling

SVM decision intuition:

\[ \hat y=\operatorname{sign}(w^\top x+b) \]

kNN intuition:

Choose k nearest documents by cosine/distance.
Predict the majority label among neighbours.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
For binary classification:

Quantity Meaning TP predicted positive and truly positive FP predicted positive but truly negative FN predicted negative but truly positive TN predicted negative and truly negative \[ \operatorname{Precision}=\frac{TP}{TP+FP} \] \[ \operatorname{Recall}=\frac{TP}{TP+FN} \] \[ F_1=\frac{2PR}{P+R} \] \[ \operatorname{Accuracy}=\frac{TP+TN}{TP+FP+FN+TN} \]

Use precision when false positives are costly; use recall when false negatives are costly. In imbalanced data, accuracy can be misleading.

docs.title: Classification Answer Pattern
docs.text:
For a method/comparison question:

  1. Define input, label set and feature representation.
  2. State the classifier objective or decision rule.
  3. State one assumption.
  4. State one strength and one weakness.
  5. Choose evaluation metric based on error cost.

docs.title: Classification Exam Traps
docs.text:
• Reporting training accuracy as final performance.
  • Saying BoW has no order but forgetting n-gram features can partially recover local order.
  • Using accuracy only for imbalanced data.
  • Confusing precision and recall denominators.
  • Treating Naive Bayes independence assumption as a claim that words are truly independent.
  • Forgetting smoothing in Naive Bayes when a word is unseen in a class.
  • Comparing classifiers without specifying features; different features can change the result more than the model family.

docs.title: 7. POS Tagging
docs.text:
POS tagging（词性标注）为句子中的每个 token 分配一个 grammatical category，因此属于 token-level classification / sequence labelling：

\[ w_{1:n}\longrightarrow t_{1:n} \]

同一 word type 的 POS 取决于 context。例如：

Time/NOUN flies/VERB like/PREP an/DET arrow/NOUN
Fruit/NOUN flies/NOUN like/VERB a/DET banana/NOUN

Claim: POS is assigned to a token in context, not permanently to a word type.

docs.title: Penn Treebank 高频标签
docs.text:
Tag Meaning Tag Meaning NN/NNS singular/plural common noun NNP/NNPS singular/plural proper noun VB base verb VBP/VBZ present verb VBD past tense VBG/VBN gerund/past participle JJ/JJR/JJS adjective/comparative/superlative RB/RBR/RBS adverb/comparative/superlative DT determiner IN preposition/subordinating conjunction PRP/PRP$ personal/possessive pronoun MD modal CC coordinating conjunction CD cardinal number RP particle TO to 
CATS/NNS SHOULD/MD CATCH/VB MICE/NNS EASILY/RB

MD 后通常接 base verb，因此 catch 标为 VB。

docs.title: Rule-based Tagger
docs.text:
1. 从 lexicon 或 tagged corpus 获取每个词的候选 tags。
  2. 用 context rules 排除不合理标签。
  3. 重复应用规则，直到留下单一 tag。
the/DT walk/{NN,VB}
Rule: If DT precedes the word, eliminate VB.
Result: the/DT walk/NN
  • 优点：可直接编码 linguistic knowledge。
  • 缺点：大型系统需要数千条 constraints，构建和维护成本高。

docs.title: Unigram Tagger
docs.text:
对每个 word type 选择训练语料中最常见的 tag：

\[ \hat t(w)=\arg\max_t C(w,t) \] 
C(book, NN)=80, C(book, VB)=20
=> always predict book/NN
  • 本质：word -> most frequent tag lookup table。
  • 讲义结果：约 90% accuracy，可解决约 75% 的 ambiguity。
  • 强 baseline，但完全忽略 context，因此会误标 I will book/VB a ticket。

docs.title: N-gram Tagger and Backoff
docs.text:
N-gram tagger 利用局部 token/tag history，例如 previous tag：

\[ \hat t_i=\arg\max_{t_i}P(t_i\mid t_{i-1},w_i) \] 
should/MD catch/?

训练数据中 MD -> VB 常见，因此 context 支持 catch/VB。Higher-order taggers 使用更多 context，但也更 sparse；workshop 中未加 backoff 的 n-gram tagger甚至可能比 unigram 更差。

Trigram -> Bigram -> Unigram -> Default tag

docs.title: Classifier-based Tagger
docs.text:
使用 Logistic Regression、Neural Network 等 discriminative classifier，逐个预测 token tag。常见 features：

target word; previous/next word; previous predicted tag;
prefix/suffix; capitalisation; digit/hyphen patterns

例如预测 CATCH 时可使用：

word=catch, previous_word=should, previous_tag=MD, suffix=ch

Error propagation: 如果 previous predicted tag 错误，它会作为错误 feature 影响后续预测。

docs.title: HMM Tagger
docs.text:
Hidden Markov Model 把 POS tags 视为 hidden states，把 tokens 视为 observations。最优 tag sequence：

\[ \hat t_{1:n} = \arg\max_{t_{1:n}} \prod_{i=1}^{n} P(t_i\mid t_{i-1})P(w_i\mid t_i) \]

需要从 tagged corpus 估计：

Parameter Meaning Formula \(\pi(t)\) initial tag probability \(P(t_1=t)\) \(A_{u,v}\) transition probability \(P(t_i=v\mid t_{i-1}=u)\) \(B_t(w)\) emission probability \(P(w_i=w\mid t_i=t)\)

两个核心假设：

  • Markov assumption: 当前 tag 只依赖 previous tag。
  • Output independence assumption: 当前 word 只依赖 current tag。

易混： transition 是 P(tag | previous tag)；emission 是 P(word | tag)。

[!example]- HMM 参数估计：silver wheels turn

Tagged corpus：

silver-JJ | wheels-NNS | turn-VBP
wheels-NNS | turn-VBP | right-JJ
right-JJ | wheels-NNS | turn-VBP

Initial probabilities：

\[ \pi(JJ)=2/3,\qquad \pi(NNS)=1/3 \]

Transition probabilities：

\[ P(NNS\mid JJ)=2/2,\quad P(VBP\mid NNS)=3/3,\quad P(JJ\mid VBP)=1/1 \]

Emission probabilities：

\[ P(right\mid JJ)=2/3,\quad P(silver\mid JJ)=1/3 \] \[ P(wheels\mid NNS)=1,\qquad P(turn\mid VBP)=1 \]

计算 transition denominator 时，不计 sentence-final tag 的无后继出现，否则 transition row 无法构成和为 1 的 probability distribution。

docs.title: Viterbi Decoding
docs.text:
逐词 greedy 选择最高概率 tag 不保证得到 globally best sequence。Viterbi 使用 dynamic programming：

\[ \operatorname{dp}[i,t] = \max_{t'} \operatorname{dp}[i-1,t'] P(t\mid t')P(w_i\mid t) \]
  1. Initialization: \(\pi(t)P(w_1\mid t)\)。
  2. Recursion: 对每个 current tag 比较所有 previous tags，并保存最大值和 backpointer。
  3. Termination: 选择最后位置分数最高的 tag。
  4. Backtrace: 沿 backpointers 恢复完整 tag sequence。

若 tagset 大小为 \(T\)、句长为 \(W\)：

\[ \text{Time complexity}=O(T^2W) \]

Claim: Viterbi efficiently finds the globally most probable HMM state sequence.

[!example]- Viterbi 手算：THEY FISH

给定 emission probabilities：

Tag they fish N 0.7 0.3 V 0.4 0.6

给定 transition probabilities：

From \ To N V <s> 0.6 0.4 N 0.8 0.2 V 0.7 0.3

1. Initialization：

\[ V_1(N)=P(N\mid<s>)P(\text{they}\mid N)=0.6\times0.7=0.42 \] \[ V_1(V)=P(V\mid<s>)P(\text{they}\mid V)=0.4\times0.4=0.16 \]

2. Recursion：计算 fish/N。

\[ \begin{aligned} N\rightarrow N &: 0.42\times0.8\times0.3=0.1008\\ V\rightarrow N &: 0.16\times0.7\times0.3=0.0336 \end{aligned} \]

因此：

\[ V_2(N)=0.1008,\qquad Back_2(N)=N \]

3. Recursion：计算 fish/V。

\[ \begin{aligned} N\rightarrow V &: 0.42\times0.2\times0.6=0.0504\\ V\rightarrow V &: 0.16\times0.3\times0.6=0.0288 \end{aligned} \]

因此：

\[ V_2(V)=0.0504,\qquad Back_2(V)=N \]

4. Termination + Backtrace：

最后一列中 \(0.1008>0.0504\)，选择 fish/N；其 backpointer 指向 they/N。因此题目给定概率下的 optimal sequence 是：

they/N fish/N

Exam trap：按题目给出的 probabilities 计算，不要因为语言直觉而擅自改成 they/N fish/V。每个非首列 cell 都必须比较所有 previous tags，并记录最大路径的 backpointer。

docs.title: Unknown Words
docs.text:
训练中未见的词需要 smoothing 或可泛化的 word-form features：

Evidence Example inference suffix -ly likely RB suffix -ed likely VBD/VBN capitalisation likely NNP numeric pattern likely CD hapax statistics unseen words often noun, then verb; rarely determiner subword morphology use common prefixes/affixes

未知词在 morphologically rich languages 中尤其严重。

docs.title: POS Method Comparison
docs.text: Method Context Global decoding Main weakness Rule-based hand-written context no costly rule construction Unigram none no cannot resolve contextual ambiguity N-gram tagger local history no sparsity; needs backoff Classifier-based flexible local features usually no error propagation HMM + Viterbi tag sequence + lexical evidence yes strong independence assumptions

docs.title: POS Exam Traps
docs.text:
• 把 word type 当作具有永久 POS；实际 tag 依赖 token context。
  • 混淆 VBD（past tense）与 VBN（past participle）。
  • 混淆 transition \(P(t_i\mid t_{i-1})\) 与 emission \(P(w_i\mid t_i)\)。
  • HMM 中只选择每个位置的 locally best tag，而没有执行 Viterbi/backtrace。
  • 计算 transition 时把 sentence-final occurrence 也放进 denominator。
  • Unknown word 的 emission 直接设为 0，导致所有相关 sequence score 为 0。

docs.title: 思想
docs.text:
FFNN（Feedforward Neural Network / MLP）将输入经过若干个 weighted linear transformation 和 nonlinear activation，最后输出分类概率。信息只从 input 向 output 前进，没有 recurrent state。

\[ h=\phi(Wx+b) \]
  • \(x\)：input features 或拼接后的 embeddings。
  • \(W,b\)：训练得到的 parameters。
  • \(\phi\)：非线性 activation，如 tanh 或 ReLU。
  • Binary classification 常用 sigmoid；mutually exclusive multiclass classification 常用 softmax。

Claim: nonlinear hidden layers learn useful feature combinations；如果只堆叠 linear layers，整体仍等价于一个 linear transformation。

docs.title: 基本算法
docs.text:
1. 将输入表示成 vector。文本分类可用 BoW/TF-IDF；FFNN LM 使用固定窗口内的 word embeddings。
  2. 逐层 forward propagation：
\[ h_1=\phi(W_1x+b_1),\qquad h_2=\phi(W_2h_1+b_2) \]
  1. 输出 logits，并转成概率：
\[ \hat y=\operatorname{softmax}(W_3h_2) \]
  1. 对正确类别计算 negative log-likelihood：
\[ \mathcal L=-\log P(y_{\mathrm{gold}}\mid x) \]
  1. 用 backpropagation 计算 gradients，再用 gradient descent 更新 \(W,b\)。
  2. 使用 L1/L2 或 dropout 减少 overfitting。

FFNN language model 将前 \(k\) 个词的 embeddings 拼接后预测下一个词：

\[ x=v_{w_{i-k}}\oplus\cdots\oplus v_{w_{i-1}}, \qquad P(w_i\mid x)=\operatorname{softmax}(W_oh) \]

其 context window 仍固定，只是 embeddings 让相似词能够共享统计信息。

docs.title: 优缺点
docs.text: 优点 缺点 可学习 nonlinear feature combinations 输入维度和 context length 通常固定 比 classical models 少依赖手工 feature engineering 不保存 sequence state，无法自然处理任意长度历史 各样本/窗口可并行计算 vocabulary-driven input/output matrices 参数量大 Embeddings 可在相似词之间共享信息 data hungry，容易 overfit，训练比 classical ML 慢 架构灵活，可用于 classification、LM、tagging FFNN LM 仍无法直接捕捉窗口外依赖

docs.title: 思想
docs.text:
RNN（Recurrent Neural Network）按顺序处理 tokens，用 hidden state \(h_t\) 压缩此前已处理的 context。所有 time steps 共享同一组参数，因此可以处理 variable-length sequences。

\[ h_t=\tanh(W_hh_{t-1}+W_xx_t+b) \] \[ y_t=\operatorname{softmax}(W_yh_t) \]

Claim: RNN theoretically has access to arbitrarily long left context, but a simple RNN does not reliably retain long-range dependencies in practice。

docs.title: 基本算法
docs.text:
1. 初始化 hidden state，通常 \(h_0=\mathbf 0\)。
  2. 对 \(t=1,\ldots,T\)：
  3. lookup 当前 token embedding \(x_t\)；
  4. 用 \(x_t\) 和 \(h_{t-1}\) 计算 \(h_t\)；
  5. 根据任务从 \(h_t\) 计算输出 \(y_t\)。
  6. Language model 中，\(x_t\) 是当前词，\(y_t\) 预测下一个词：
\[ P(w_{t+1}\mid w_{1:t})=\operatorname{softmax}(W_yh_t) \]
  1. 累加各 time step 的 loss：
\[ \mathcal L=-\sum_t\log P(w_{t+1}^{\mathrm{gold}}\mid w_{1:t}) \]
  1. 将 RNN 沿时间展开，使用 BPTT（Backpropagation Through Time），汇总共享参数在所有 time steps 上的 gradients。
  2. Generation 时把生成的 token 作为下一步输入，形成 autoregressive decoding。

docs.title: 优缺点
docs.text: 优点 缺点 可处理 variable-length input time steps 必须 sequentially computed，难以并行 Hidden state 保留 word order 和 prefix information BPTT 路径长，训练较慢 参数跨时间共享，不随 sequence length 增长 容易出现 vanishing/exploding gradients 可用于 LM、text classification、sequence labelling 理论上的无限 context 不等于实践中能记住长期信息 比固定窗口 FFNN 更自然地表示 sequence Autoregressive generation 有 train-test mismatch 和 error propagation

docs.title: 思想
docs.text:
LSTM（Long Short-Term Memory）是带有 gated memory cell 的 RNN。Cell state \(C_t\) 提供较直接的信息与 gradient 通路；forget、input、output gates 控制旧信息删除、新信息写入和当前信息输出。

Claim: LSTM mitigates vanishing gradients and preserves long-range information better than a simple RNN, but it does not guarantee perfect memory of arbitrarily long context。

docs.title: 基本算法
docs.text:
给定当前输入 \(x_t\)、前一 hidden state \(h_{t-1}\) 和前一 cell state \(C_{t-1}\)：

  1. Forget gate：保留多少旧记忆
\[ f_t=\sigma(W_f[h_{t-1},x_t]+b_f) \]
  1. Input gate：写入多少新信息
\[ i_t=\sigma(W_i[h_{t-1},x_t]+b_i) \]
  1. Candidate memory：准备写入的内容
\[ \widetilde C_t=\tanh(W_C[h_{t-1},x_t]+b_C) \]
  1. Update cell state
\[ C_t=f_t\odot C_{t-1}+i_t\odot\widetilde C_t \]
  1. Output gate：暴露多少 memory
\[ o_t=\sigma(W_o[h_{t-1},x_t]+b_o) \]
  1. Update hidden state
\[ h_t=o_t\odot\tanh(C_t) \]

其中 \(\sigma\) 将 gate 元素限制在 \([0,1]\)，\(\odot\) 表示 element-wise multiplication。

记忆口诀：

forget = keep old
input  = write new
output = expose memory

不要混淆：

  • \(C_t\)：较长期的 cell state / memory。
  • \(h_t\)：当前位置向下一步和输出层提供的 hidden state。

docs.title: 优缺点
docs.text: 优点 缺点 比 simple RNN 更能保留 long-range dependencies 仍必须 sequentially process tokens Gated cell path 缓解 vanishing gradients 每步有多个 gates，参数和计算量更大 可学习何时 forget、write、expose information 比 simple RNN 慢，也难以高度并行 适合 LM、classification、POS/NER 等 sequence tasks 很长序列上仍可能遗忘，不能彻底解决 long context 可扩展为 stacked 或 bidirectional LSTM Bidirectional LSTM 使用 future context，不适合 causal generation

docs.title: 11. FFNN vs RNN vs LSTM
docs.text: 模型 核心状态 Context 训练方式 最大优势 主要弱点 FFNN 无 recurrent state 固定输入/窗口 ordinary backpropagation 简单、并行、灵活 无法自然表示任意长度 sequence Simple RNN hidden state \(h_t\) 理论上整个 prefix BPTT 参数共享并处理 variable length vanishing gradient、sequential LSTM hidden \(h_t\) + cell \(C_t\) 更可靠的长期 prefix BPTT through gates 门控记忆缓解长期依赖问题 更慢、更复杂、仍 sequential

docs.title: Neural Network Exam Traps
docs.text:
• 认为 FFNN 堆叠多个 linear layers 就自动获得 nonlinearity；必须有 nonlinear activation。
  • Multiclass softmax 的 denominator 漏掉其他所有 classes。
  • 把 FFNN LM 当作无限 context model；它仍使用 fixed window。
  • 认为 RNN 的 hidden state 能无损保存整个历史；它只是有限维压缩表示。
  • 忘记 RNN 在所有 time steps 共享 \(W_h,W_x,W_y\)。
  • 把 ordinary backpropagation 和 BPTT 当作不同优化原理；BPTT 是对 unrolled RNN 应用 backpropagation。
  • 混淆 LSTM 的 \(C_t\) 与 \(h_t\)，或混淆 forget/input/output gates 的职责。
  • 把 gate multiplication 写成普通 matrix multiplication；这里是 element-wise \(\odot\)。
  • 认为 LSTM 完全消除了 vanishing gradient 或可以完美记忆无限 context。
  • 使用 bidirectional LSTM 做 causal next-token generation，导致 future information leakage。

docs.title: Q/K/V Projections
docs.text:
给定一组 token representations：

\[ X\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times d_{\mathrm{model}}} \]

通过三个独立的 learned linear projections 得到：

\[ Q=XW_Q,\qquad K=XW_K,\qquad V=XW_V \] 向量 结构性角色 直觉 Query \(q_i\) 位置 \(i\) 发起匹配 当前 token 正在寻找什么 Key \(k_j\) 位置 \(j\) 接受匹配 当前 token 可用什么特征被找到 Value \(v_j\) 匹配后传递内容 被关注后实际提供什么信息

Q/K/V 不是三种不同 token，而是同一输入通过不同参数得到的 representations。计算图使 Q/K 负责 routing、V 负责 content transfer；具体特征由 downstream loss 通过 gradient descent 学习。

docs.title: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
docs.text:
单个 query 对 key \(j\) 的 compatibility score：

\[ s_{ij}=q_i^\top k_j \]

完整 attention：

\[ \operatorname{Attention}(Q,K,V) = \operatorname{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}+M\right)V \]

计算顺序：

  1. \(QK^\top\)：计算所有 query-key similarities。
  2. 除以 \(\sqrt{d_k}\)：避免 dot products 随维度增大，使 softmax 过度饱和。
  3. 加 mask \(M\)：按架构屏蔽无效或未来位置。
  4. 对每个 query 的 key scores 做 softmax，得到 weights。
  5. 对 value vectors 加权求和，生成 contextual representation。

若 \(Q,K\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times d_k}\)、\(V\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times d_v}\)：

\[ QK^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times N}, \qquad \operatorname{Attention}(Q,K,V)\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times d_v} \]

Claim: Q/K 决定从哪里读取，V 决定读取什么。若省略 learned \(W_V\) 并直接加权 \(X\)，相当于固定 \(V=X\)，表达能力较弱。

docs.title: Self-Attention
docs.text:
Self-attention: Q、K、V 都来自同一个 sequence：

\[ Q=XW_Q,\qquad K=XW_K,\qquad V=XW_V \]

每个 token 根据同一序列中的其他 tokens 构建 contextual representation：

\[ h_i=\sum_j\alpha_{ij}v_j \]

其中 \(\alpha_{ij}\) 是位置 \(i\) 对位置 \(j\) 的 attention weight。与 static embedding 不同，同一 word type 在不同句子中可产生不同输出表示。

docs.title: Self-Attention vs Cross-Attention
docs.text:
类型 Query 来源 Key/Value 来源 用途 Self-attention 当前 sequence 同一 sequence 建模序列内部关系 Cross-attention decoder/current sequence encoder/另一 sequence 根据输入条件生成输出

Transformer encoder-decoder 中，decoder cross-attention 使用：

Q = decoder hidden states
K,V = final encoder output sequence

易错点：attention 是总称；self-attention 和 cross-attention 由 Q/K/V 的来源区分。

docs.title: Multi-Head Attention
docs.text:
单一 attention head 可能难以同时表示 syntax、semantics、position 和 coreference。Multi-head attention 使用多组独立 projections：

\[ \operatorname{head}_r = \operatorname{Attention}(XW_Q^{(r)},XW_K^{(r)},XW_V^{(r)}) \] \[ \operatorname{MultiHead}(X) = \operatorname{Concat}(\operatorname{head}_1,\ldots,\operatorname{head}_H)W_O \]
  • 每个 head 在不同 representation subspace 中独立计算 attention。
  • 上式是 self-attention；cross-attention 则分别从 decoder states 和 encoder outputs 投影 Q 与 K/V。
  • Heads 可以学习不同关系，但不保证每个 head 都有清晰、唯一的人类语言学解释。
  • Concatenation 后使用 \(W_O\) 混合各 head 的信息并投影回 \(d_{\mathrm{model}}\)。

docs.title: Masked/Causal Self-Attention
docs.text:
Decoder-only LM 预测 next token 时不能看到未来 tokens。Causal mask 在 softmax 前将未来 scores 设为 \(-\infty\)：

\[ M_{ij}= \begin{cases} 0,&j\le i\\ -\infty,&j>i \end{cases} \]

Softmax 后，被 mask 的未来位置权重为 0。

架构 Attention visibility BERT encoder bidirectional/full self-attention GPT decoder causal/masked self-attention，只看左侧和当前位置 Encoder-decoder decoder causal self-attention + encoder cross-attention

训练时完整 target sequence 已知，mask 可一次应用到整个 \(N\times N\) score matrix，因此所有位置仍可并行训练；autoregressive inference 仍需逐 token 生成。

docs.title: Positional Information
docs.text:
Self-attention 的 query-key comparison 本身不编码 token order，因此输入需要加入 positional representation：

\[ x_i=e_{\mathrm{token},i}+e_{\mathrm{position},i} \]

原始 Transformer 使用 deterministic sinusoidal encoding；不同维度使用不同频率，使位置在多个尺度上表示。相加保持 \(d_{\mathrm{model}}\) 不变，后续 learned projections 可同时利用 token 和 position signals。

docs.title: Why Transformer Training Is Parallel
docs.text:
RNN 必须按顺序计算 \(h_i=f(h_{i-1},x_i)\)。Transformer 没有跨 token 的 recurrent state transfer，而是用矩阵运算同时计算：

\[ Q=XW_Q,\quad K=XW_K,\quad V=XW_V,\quad QK^\top \]

因此同一层内的所有 positions 和 attention heads 可以批量处理。Transformer blocks 之间仍须逐层执行。

docs.title: Attention Exam Traps
docs.text:
• 把 Q/K/V 当成三种 token；它们是输入的不同 learned projections。
  • 认为 attention weights 直接加权 keys；最终被加权求和的是 values。
  • softmax 对整个矩阵统一归一化；实际对每个 query 对应的一行 key scores 归一化。
  • 忘记除以 \(\sqrt{d_k}\)，或误写为 \(\sqrt{d_{\mathrm{model}}}\)。
  • 认为 self-attention 自动知道词序；必须加入 positional information。
  • 混淆 self-attention 与 cross-attention 的 Q/K/V 来源。
  • 认为 causal masking 导致训练不能并行；mask 可对完整 attention matrix 一次应用。
  • 认为 multi-head 只是重复相同 attention；每个 head 有独立 projections，并在不同 subspace 中计算。
  • 把 attention head 当成必然可解释的语言学规则；head behaviour 不保证唯一或清晰。
  • 认为 Transformer inference 也完全并行；autoregressive decoding 仍依赖先前生成的 tokens。

docs.title: Distributional Hypothesis
docs.text:
Distributional hypothesis：

You shall know a word by the company it keeps.

含义相似的词倾向于出现在相似 context 中。讲义区分：

  • Document as context：主要反映 topic association，例如 voting 与 politics。
  • Local word window as context：更直接反映 lexical meaning，例如 eat a pizza 与 eat a burger。

将每个词在不同 contexts 中的出现情况写成一行数字，就得到 distributional word vector。

Claim: word meaning can be approximated from patterns of contextual co-occurrence in unlabelled text。

docs.title: Representation Pipeline
docs.text:
讲义中的 embedding 方法分为两条路线：

Count-based:
co-occurrence counts
→ weighting (TF-IDF or PMI/PPMI)
→ SVD
→ low-dimensional dense vectors

Neural:
context-prediction task
→ Skip-gram or CBOW
→ negative sampling
→ learned dense vectors

注意：TF-IDF 和 PPMI matrix 本身通常仍是 sparse representation；经过 truncated SVD 后才得到较短的 dense embeddings。

docs.title: Term-Document Matrix
docs.text:
以 document 作为 context，建立：

\[ A\in\mathbb R^{|V|\times |D|} \]
  • Row：一个 word 在所有 documents 中的分布，可作为高维 word vector。
  • Column：一个 document 中各 words 的分布，可作为 document vector。
  • Cell \(A_{w,d}\)：词 \(w\) 在文档 \(d\) 中的 frequency 或 weighted frequency。

原始 term-document matrix 通常 high-dimensional and sparse，并且容易被 common words 支配。

docs.title: TF-IDF
docs.text:
TF-IDF（Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency）提高“当前文档中常见、整个 corpus 中罕见”的词的权重，并降低 corpus-wide common words 的权重。

讲义给出的 IDF：

\[ \operatorname{idf}(w) = \log\frac{|D|}{\operatorname{df}(w)} \]

其中 \(\operatorname{df}(w)\) 是包含 \(w\) 的文档数。最终：

\[ \operatorname{tfidf}(w,d) = \operatorname{tf}(w,d)\operatorname{idf}(w) \]

算法：

  1. 建立 term-document count matrix。
  2. 计算每个词的 document frequency。
  3. 计算 IDF。
  4. 每个 cell 用 TF × IDF 重新加权。

若一个词出现在所有文档中：

\[ \operatorname{idf}(w)=\log\frac{|D|}{|D|}=0 \]

所以无论它在某文档中出现多少次，TF-IDF 都为 0。

[!example]- TF-IDF 例子

假设 corpus 有 100 篇文档，cat 在当前文档出现 3 次、在整个 corpus 的 5 篇文档中出现：

\[ \operatorname{tfidf}(\text{cat},d) = 3\log\frac{100}{5} = 3\log20 \]

若 the 在当前文档出现 10 次，但出现在全部 100 篇文档：

\[ \operatorname{tfidf}(\text{the},d) = 10\log\frac{100}{100} = 0 \]

the 的 raw count 更高，但没有 document-discriminative value。

docs.title: Singular Value Decomposition
docs.text:
SVD（Singular Value Decomposition）将矩阵分解为：

\[ A=U\Sigma V^T \]

对于 term-document matrix：

  • \(U\)：新的 term dimensions；
  • \(\Sigma\)：按重要性排列的 singular values；
  • \(V^T\)：新的 document dimensions；
  • \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=m\) 时，完整分解有 \(m\) 个 latent dimensions。

Truncated SVD / Latent Semantic Analysis（LSA）只保留最大的前 \(k\) 个 singular values：

\[ A\approx U_k\Sigma_kV_k^T \]

\(U_k\) 的每一行可作为一个词的 \(k\)-dimensional dense representation。讲义给出的典型 \(k\) 为 100-5000。

作用：

  • sparse \(\rightarrow\) dense；
  • 减少 features、storage 和 computation；
  • 丢弃较弱 dimensions，减少 noise 和 overfitting；
  • 给出原矩阵的 best rank-\(k\) approximation。

Claim: SVD does not randomly delete features; it preserves the strongest latent dimensions measured by singular values。

docs.title: Word-Context Matrix
docs.text:
以 neighbouring words 作为 context，在固定窗口中统计 target-context co-occurrence：

\[ A_{w,c}=C(w,c) \]

例如窗口中经常出现：

heaven ... hell

则 heaven 的向量在 hell context dimension 上有较高 count。

Raw frequency 的问题是 the 等 common words 会支配所有 vectors。这里 context 是词而非文档，因此讲义使用 PMI，而不是普通 TF-IDF。

docs.title: PMI and PPMI
docs.text:
PMI（Pointwise Mutual Information）比较实际 joint probability 与独立假设下的 expected probability：

\[ \operatorname{PMI}(x,y) = \log_2\frac{P(x,y)}{P(x)P(y)} \]

由 count matrix 计算：

\[ P(x,y)=\frac{C(x,y)}{N}, \qquad P(x)=\frac{C(x,*)}{N}, \qquad P(y)=\frac{C(*,y)}{N} \]

解释：

PMI 意义 \(>0\) co-occur 比 independence 预期更频繁 \(=0\) 接近 independent \(<0\) co-occur 比预期更少

讲义的 state 与 country：

\[ C(\text{state,country})=10,\quad C(\text{state},*)=12786,\quad C(*,\text{country})=3617,\quad N=15871304 \] \[ \operatorname{PMI}(\text{state,country}) \approx 1.78 \]

表示两词共同出现得比 independence 预期更频繁。

PPMI（Positive PMI）：

\[ \operatorname{PPMI}(x,y) = \max(\operatorname{PMI}(x,y),0) \]

将 negative associations 截断为 0。PPMI matrix 仍可再使用 SVD 得到 dense vectors。

docs.title: Count-Based Embedding Algorithms
docs.text:
Context Initial matrix Weighting Dense representation Document Term-document counts TF-IDF Truncated SVD / LSA Local words Word-context counts PMI / PPMI Truncated SVD

共同优点：

  • 从 unlabelled corpus 学习；
  • counts 和 dimensions 可解释；
  • 不需要训练复杂 neural network。

共同缺点：

  • 原始矩阵巨大且 sparse；
  • 对 window、context definition 和 weighting choice 敏感；
  • 构建和分解大型矩阵成本高；
  • 得到的是 static word-type representation。

docs.title: Word2Vec
docs.text:
Word2Vec 设计一个 context-prediction neural task，主要目标就是学习 word vectors：

  • Unsupervised：训练标签直接来自 raw text 的窗口。
  • Efficient：使用 negative sampling 避免 full-vocabulary softmax。

核心仍是 distributional hypothesis：真实 target-context pairs 应有较高 vector similarity。

docs.title: Skip-Gram
docs.text:
Skip-gram：给定 target word，预测 surrounding context words。

原句：

Bereft of life he rests in peace

若 target 是 rests、window size \(L=2\)，训练预测：

P(life | rests)
P(he | rests)
P(in | rests)
P(peace | rests)

总目标：

\[ \prod_{\ell\in\{-L,\ldots,-1,1,\ldots,L\}} P(w_{t+\ell}\mid w_t) \]

Full-softmax probability：

\[ P(c\mid w) = \frac{\exp(W_w\cdot C_c)} {\sum_{u\in V}\exp(W_w\cdot C_u)} \]
  • \(W_w\)：target/word embedding；
  • \(C_c\)：context embedding；
  • dot product 越大，模型认为 pair 越合理。

Skip-gram 学习两个 matrices：target matrix \(W\) 和 context matrix \(C\)。同一个 word type 在两个角色中有不同参数。

docs.title: CBOW
docs.text:
CBOW（Continuous Bag of Words）：给定 surrounding context words，预测 target word。

对于：

life he [rests] in peace

CBOW 使用：

life, he, in, peace → rests

先对 context embeddings 求和或平均形成 context representation，再预测中心词。

对比 Skip-gram CBOW Input target word surrounding context words Output context words target word 一个窗口的预测 多个 一个 记忆 target \(\rightarrow\) context context \(\rightarrow\) target

docs.title: Negative Sampling
docs.text:
Full softmax 的 denominator 对 vocabulary 中每个词求和，\(|V|\) 很大时训练太慢。Negative sampling 将问题改成 binary classification：

(rests, life)     → positive / real context
(rests, aardvark) → negative / noise word

正样本概率：

\[ P(+\mid w,c)=\sigma(W_w\cdot C_c) \]

负样本概率：

\[ P(-\mid w,n)=\sigma(-W_w\cdot C_n) \]

每个 positive pair 搭配 \(k\) 个随机 negative samples：

\[ \mathcal L = \log\sigma(W_w\cdot C_c) + \sum_{i=1}^{k} \log\sigma(-W_w\cdot C_{n_i}) \]

训练效果：

  • 提高真实 target-context pairs 的 similarity；
  • 降低 target-noise pairs 的 similarity；
  • 每个 example 只更新少量 sampled words，不需遍历完整 vocabulary。

Claim: negative sampling is an efficiency approximation for learning embeddings, not a method for constructing all possible negative pairs。

docs.title: Static Embeddings
docs.text:
TF-IDF/SVD、PPMI/SVD 和 Word2Vec 都为每个 word type 提供一个固定向量：

bank in "bank account"
bank in "river bank"

两处 bank 使用同一个 static embedding，无法直接根据句子区分 word sense。后续 pretrained Transformer 产生的 contextual embeddings 会让同一个词在不同 context 中拥有不同向量。

docs.title: Cosine Similarity
docs.text:
\[ \cos(x,y) = \frac{x\cdot y}{\|x\|\|y\|} \]

比较 vector direction，而不主要受 magnitude 影响。Word similarity evaluation 将模型 cosine scores 与人工 judgement 比较。

讲义数据集：

  • WordSim-353：主要是 nouns 的 relatedness；
  • SimLex-999：包含 nouns、verbs、adjectives。

docs.title: Word Analogy
docs.text:
讲义例子：

Man : King :: Woman : ?
\[ v(?)=v(\text{Woman})-v(\text{Man})+v(\text{King}) \]

寻找与结果 cosine similarity 最高的 word，预期为 Queen。这说明某些 lexical relations 在 embedding space 中呈现近似 linear geometry。

docs.title: Downstream Evaluation
docs.text:
最实用的评估是在 downstream task 中使用 embeddings：

  • 将 word embeddings 求和/平均作为 classifier features；
  • 用 pretrained vectors 初始化 neural model 的 embedding layer；
  • 检查是否改善 classification、tagging 等最终指标。

讲义结论：neural embeddings 通常优于 count-based vectors；pretrained word vectors 是有效初始化，并进一步引出 whole-model pretraining。

docs.title: Embedding Method Comparison
docs.text: 方法 Context Output 核心优势 主要限制 TF-IDF document sparse word/document vectors 简单、可解释、降低 common words 高维、无 semantic sharing SVD/LSA weighted count matrix dense low-rank vectors 降维、去噪、latent structure 分解大矩阵成本高 PMI/PPMI local co-occurrence weighted sparse vectors 衡量超出 independence 的关联 仍是高维 sparse matrix PPMI + SVD local context dense vectors 结合 association weighting 与降维 依赖 count/window design Skip-gram target \(\rightarrow\) context dense static embeddings 擅长学习局部语义关系 full softmax 昂贵 CBOW context \(\rightarrow\) target dense static embeddings 每个窗口只预测中心词，效率高 context 被 bagged，内部顺序丢失 Negative sampling real vs noise pairs efficient Word2Vec training 避免完整 vocabulary normalisation 依赖 negative sampling strategy

docs.title: Embedding Exam Traps
docs.text:
• 把 distributional similarity 当成 dictionary definition；它由 observed usage patterns 近似得到。
  • 混淆 document context 与 local word-window context。
  • 混淆 TF 与 DF：DF 是包含该词的文档数，不是 total token count。
  • 把 TF-IDF 当成天然 dense embedding；它通常仍是 sparse weighted vector。
  • 认为 SVD 随机删列；truncated SVD 保留最大的 singular-value dimensions。
  • PMI 直接使用 raw counts 代入比值，而没有先转换成 joint/marginal probabilities。
  • 看到 negative PMI 时忘记 PPMI 要截断为 0。
  • 颠倒 Skip-gram 与 CBOW 的预测方向。
  • 忘记 Skip-gram 有 target matrix \(W\) 和 context matrix \(C\)。
  • 把 negative sampling 理解为对全部 non-context words 训练；实际只抽取 \(k\) 个 noise words。
  • 把 cosine similarity 写成 dot product，漏掉两个 vector norms。
  • 认为 static embedding 可以为同一 word type 的不同 senses 产生不同向量。
  • 只用 analogy 判断 embedding 好坏；downstream evaluation 更能反映实际用途。

docs.title: Pretrained Vectors vs Pretrained Networks
docs.text:
• Pretrained word vectors: 只预训练 embedding matrix，例如 Word2Vec；下游模型的其余参数仍需训练。
  • Pretrained model: 在大规模数据上预训练整个 neural network，再通过 fine-tuning 等方式适配 downstream task。
  • Claim: whole-model pretraining 不只是提供 static word vectors，还能产生 context-dependent representations。

docs.title: Encoder, Decoder, Encoder-Decoder
docs.text: 架构 Attention/context 典型能力 代表模型 Encoder-only bidirectional context understanding、classification、token labelling BERT Decoder-only left/causal context autoregressive generation GPT Encoder-decoder encoder 处理输入；decoder 根据输入生成输出 conditional generation、translation、summarisation T5

docs.title: 1. Tokenisation and Embedding
docs.text:
输入先被切分成 tokens，再通过 embedding layer 映射为模型可处理的 vectors：

text → tokens → embedding vectors

Word2Vec 可以提供 pretrained static embeddings，但不是 encoder-decoder 的必要组成。Transformer 通常学习自己的 token embedding matrix。

docs.title: 2. Encoding
docs.text:
Encoder 将 input embeddings 转换成 contextual representations。Encoder 可以由 RNN、LSTM、CNN 或 Transformer 构成。

“Encoder 输出是一个 context vector”只适用于最基础的 RNN/LSTM seq2seq 描述：

模型 Encoder output 如何传给 Decoder Basic RNN/LSTM seq2seq final hidden state；LSTM 还可能传 final cell state，形成 fixed-size context RNN/LSTM + attention 每个 decoder step 对全部 encoder hidden states 加权 Transformer encoder-decoder 保留完整 encoder output sequence，通过 cross-attention 读取

docs.title: 3. Autoregressive Decoding
docs.text:
Decoder 从 start token <s> / <BOS> 开始，不是从 end token 开始。每一步预测下一个 token：

\[ p(y\mid x)=\prod_{t=1}^{m}p(y_t\mid y_{<t},x) \] 
<BOS> → predict y1 → use previous token → predict y2 → ... → <EOS>

Transformer decoder 同时使用：

  • causal self-attention: 只能看到当前 token 左侧的 target tokens；
  • cross-attention: 读取 encoder 最后一层的完整 output sequence。

docs.title: Teacher Forcing
docs.text:
Teacher forcing：训练 decoder 时，不管上一步预测是否正确，下一步都输入正确的 gold target token。

训练：

\[ p(y_t\mid y_{<t}^{\text{gold}},x) \]

推理：

\[ p(\hat y_t\mid \hat y_{<t},x) \] 阶段 Decoder 下一步输入 Training with teacher forcing 正确的 previous gold token Inference 模型自己的 previous predicted token

即使使用 teacher forcing，每一步仍会：

  1. 预测 output distribution；
  2. 与 gold token 计算 cross-entropy loss；
  3. 只是下一步输入改用 gold token，而不是上一步 prediction。

Claim: teacher forcing 加快训练，但造成 training-inference mismatch；推理时的早期错误可能传播到后续 tokens。

docs.title: GPT-1 vs BERT vs T5
docs.text: Model Architecture Pretraining objective Downstream interface GPT-1 decoder-only next-token prediction fine-tune with task head BERT encoder-only masked LM + next sentence prediction [CLS]/token states + task head T5 encoder-decoder span corruption every task as text-to-text

docs.title: Pretrained Models Exam Traps
docs.text:
• 把 pretrained word embeddings 与 whole-model pretraining 当成同一件事。
  • 说 Word2Vec 是所有 encoder-decoder 模型的第一层；它只是可能的 embedding 初始化方式。
  • 说任何 encoder 都只输出一个 context vector；Transformer encoder 输出一组 contextual vectors。
  • 把 <EOS> 当成 decoder 的第一个输入；通常第一个输入是 <BOS> / <s>。
  • 把 teacher forcing 写成 force learning。
  • 认为 teacher forcing 不计算 prediction/loss；它只是用 gold previous token 作为下一步输入。
  • 认为 inference 也能使用 gold tokens；推理时 decoder 必须使用自己的历史输出。
  • 混淆 decoder causal self-attention 与 cross-attention。
  • 认为所有 pretrained models 都使用 next-token prediction；BERT 使用 masked LM，T5 使用 span corruption。

docs.title: In-Context Learning (ICL)
docs.text:
In-context learning：把任务描述和可选示例放入 prompt，让 pretrained LM 在推理时根据上下文完成任务，不更新模型参数。

Instruction
Input 1 → Output 1
Input 2 → Output 2
New input → ?

模型的适应发生在当前 context window 内：

  • prompt 改变了模型本次 forward pass 的条件；
  • weights 保持 frozen；
  • 对话结束或上下文被移除后，这次适应通常不会永久保存；
  • demonstrations 会占用 context window，并可能受措辞、顺序和格式影响。

Claim: ICL is adaptation through context at inference time, not learning through gradient descent.

docs.title: Zero-shot, One-shot, Few-shot
docs.text:
这里的一个 shot 指一个完整的 task demonstration，通常包含 input 和期望 output。

Setting Prompt 中的 demonstration 数量 典型格式 Zero-shot 0 instruction + new input One-shot 1 one input-output example + new input Few-shot 少量多个 several input-output examples + new input 
Zero-shot:
Translate to French: cat → ?

One-shot:
dog → chien
cat → ?

Few-shot:
dog → chien
house → maison
cat → ?

注意：

  • zero-shot 仍然可以包含自然语言 instruction；
  • one-shot 是一个示例，不是一个 token、一个类别或一次训练迭代；
  • few-shot examples 是 prompt 的一部分，不是用来做 backpropagation 的 training set；
  • “zero-shot”不表示模型预训练时从未见过相关概念，只表示当前 prompt 没有提供 demonstration。

docs.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
docs.text:
Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting：在示例中展示 intermediate reasoning steps，使模型模仿“问题 → 推理过程 → 答案”的输出结构。

Question 1 → reasoning steps → answer
Question 2 → reasoning steps → answer
New question → ?
  • Few-shot CoT: prompt 中提供带推理步骤的 demonstrations；
  • Zero-shot CoT: 不提供示例，只加入类似 “Let's think step by step” 的 reasoning cue；
  • CoT 特别适合 multi-step arithmetic、symbolic reasoning 和 compositional tasks；
  • 它生成的是推理文本，不保证每一步都忠实反映模型内部计算，也不保证答案正确。

Claim: CoT changes the prompted computation and output format; it does not update the underlying model weights.

docs.title: ICL Exam Traps
docs.text:
• 把 prompt 中的 examples 称为 fine-tuning data。
  • 认为 few-shot 会永久保存新任务。
  • 认为 zero-shot 没有 instruction。
  • 认为 one-shot 是“模型只预测一次”。
  • 认为 CoT 等于模型参数中新增了一个 reasoning module。
  • 忽略 demonstrations 会消耗 context window，并且结果可能对顺序和格式敏感。

docs.title: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)
docs.text: SFT：在 pretrained model 上使用带标签的 input-output pairs，通过 supervised loss 和 backpropagation 更新模型权重。

docs.title: SFT Data Format
docs.text:
一条 instruction-tuning demonstration 通常写成：

Prompt x:
System instruction + user instruction + optional task input

Target response y:
Human-written or curated ideal answer

例如：

Prompt:
Classify the sentiment: "The film was surprisingly good."

Target:
positive

训练前会把 prompt 和 target 拼接并 tokenise：

[BOS] prompt tokens [separator] target tokens [EOS]

通常主要在 target/assistant tokens 上计算 loss；prompt tokens 提供条件，但可以通过 loss mask 排除。具体实现也可能对整个序列计算 causal-LM loss。

对 prompt \(x\) 和目标 response \(y=(y_1,\ldots,y_T)\)，常见目标为：

\[ \mathcal{L}_{\text{SFT}} =-\sum_{t=1}^{T}\log p_\theta(y_t\mid x,y_{<t}) \]

docs.title: SFT Training Process
docs.text:
1. Start from a pretrained LM
2. Collect and clean prompt-target demonstrations
3. Format, tokenise, truncate/pad, and batch examples
4. Forward pass with prompt + gold previous target tokens
5. Compute cross-entropy on target tokens
6. Backpropagate gradients
7. Optimizer updates model parameters
8. Repeat over mini-batches and evaluate held-out prompts

训练时使用 teacher forcing。预测第 \(t\) 个 response token 时，模型看到正确的 \(y_{<t}\)，而不是自己之前生成的 token：

Prompt: Translate "cat":
Gold target: le chat

predict "le"   from prompt
predict "chat" from prompt + gold "le"
predict EOS    from prompt + gold "le chat"

每个位置都可以在同一次 forward pass 中并行计算 next-token loss，因为完整 gold sequence 已知。Inference 时 gold response 不存在，模型才需要 autoregressive generation。

docs.title: What SFT Learns
docs.text:
SFT 增加训练 target 的 token probability，因此主要学习：

  • instruction 与目标操作之间的映射；
  • 回答格式、风格和长度；
  • demonstrations 中包含的任务知识与行为；
  • 何时回答、总结、分类或按示例拒绝。

SFT 的监督信号是 absolute target：它告诉模型“模仿这个回答”，但不会直接告诉模型其他合理回答之间的相对质量。

docs.title: Why SFT Is Insufficient for Human Preferences
docs.text:
SFT 并非完全学不到安全或礼貌行为：如果 demonstrations 中包含安全拒答、诚实表达不确定性等示例，模型可以模仿它们。问题是其 objective 只提高单个 gold response 的 token probability，没有显式建模人类对多个候选回答的相对偏好。

SFT signal:
prompt x → imitate one target y*

Missing signal:
for the same x, humans prefer y_A over y_B
because y_A is safer / more helpful / more honest

因此，SFT 对安全、伦理和风格权衡的建模能力受限：

  • 一个 prompt 往往有多个 factually correct responses，但 helpfulness、tone、harmlessness 不同；
  • gold response 只说明“这个回答可以模仿”，不直接说明 rejected response 为什么较差；
  • cross-entropy 对每个 token 做 imitation，不直接表示整段回答的 holistic preference；
  • 人类偏好可能因群体、语境和规范而变化，单个 demonstration 不能完整编码这些 trade-offs；
  • demonstration 中未覆盖的安全边界，不能仅靠 SFT objective 稳定推出。

Exam claim: SFT can imitate preference-related behaviour present in demonstrations, but it does not explicitly learn relative human preferences among alternative responses.

docs.title: SFT Strengths and Limitations
docs.text:
Strength Limitation 目标函数稳定，训练方式与 language modelling 相似 高质量 ideal responses 成本高 直接学习 instruction-following format 一个 target 不能完整表示所有合理回答 比 RLHF 简单、便宜 容易继承 demonstration 的 bias、错误和风格 更新会保存在 weights 中 可能 overfit 或造成 catastrophic forgetting 为后续 preference optimisation 提供稳定 policy 不能直接表达 helpfulness/safety 等细粒度相对偏好

Claim: unlike prompting or ICL, SFT changes \(\theta\), so the adaptation persists after the prompt is removed.

docs.title: Instruction Tuning
docs.text:
Instruction tuning：在多种任务的 natural-language instruction-output pairs 上进行 SFT，使模型学会遵循指令，并泛化到未见过的任务描述。

Pretrained LM
    ↓
Collect/convert many tasks into instruction-response format
    ↓
Mix tasks and demonstrations
    ↓
Supervised fine-tuning
    ↓
Instruction-following model

Instruction tuning 是 SFT 的一种特定形式：

Concept 范围 SFT 任何使用 labelled targets 的 supervised fine-tuning Instruction tuning 使用 natural-language instructions，通常覆盖多个任务的 SFT One-task fine-tuning 只针对一个特定 downstream task 更新权重

因此：

\[ \text{Instruction tuning} \subseteq \text{SFT} \]

但不能说所有 SFT 都是 instruction tuning。

docs.title: Prompting vs Instruction Tuning
docs.text:
Property Prompting / ICL Instruction Tuning / SFT 发生阶段 inference time training/post-training time 是否更新 weights No Yes 任务信息来源 当前 prompt instruction-output training data 是否通常跨会话保留 No Yes，保存在参数中 成本 无额外训练，但占 context 需要训练算力和 labelled/synthetic data 主要风险 prompt sensitivity、context limit overfitting、data bias、catastrophic forgetting

Fast test: 如果只改 prompt，没有 optimizer/backpropagation，就是 prompting；如果使用 loss 更新 weights，就是 fine-tuning。

docs.title: FLAN
docs.text:
FLAN (Finetuned Language Net)：把多种 NLP datasets 转换为自然语言 instructions，并对 pretrained LM 做 instruction tuning。

核心思想不是为每个任务单独训练模型，而是：

  1. 将 classification、QA、translation、reasoning 等任务统一为 instruction-response format；
  2. 混合多个 tasks 和 prompt templates；
  3. 训练模型理解新的 natural-language task descriptions；
  4. 在 held-out/unseen tasks 上测试 zero-shot generalisation。

Claim: task diversity is central to instruction tuning because the goal is learning to follow instructions across tasks, not memorising one task.

docs.title: Instruction Tuning Exam Traps
docs.text:
• 把 system prompt 称为 instruction tuning；它仍然是 prompting。
  • 把 few-shot demonstrations 称为 SFT；只有执行梯度更新才是训练。
  • 认为 instruction tuning 创建了全新的 base model；它从 pretrained model 继续训练。
  • 认为所有 SFT 都是 instruction tuning。
  • 认为 instruction tuning 保证 factuality 或 safety；它主要学习目标回答格式和 instruction-following behaviour。

docs.title: 17. Alpaca
docs.text: Stanford Alpaca：使用较强的 teacher model 生成 instruction-following data，再对 LLaMA 7B 做 SFT 的低成本 instruction-tuning 方法。

docs.title: Data Generation and Training Pipeline
docs.text:
175 human-written seed tasks
            ↓
Teacher LM generates new instructions, inputs, and outputs
            ↓
Filter and deduplicate
            ↓
About 52K instruction-following examples
            ↓
SFT of LLaMA 7B
            ↓
Alpaca instruction-following model

每条数据大致包含：

instruction: Describe the following concept...
input: optional additional task input
output: desired response

Alpaca 展示了 self-instruct / synthetic instruction data 的价值：少量人工 seeds 可以通过强模型扩展成大规模训练集。

docs.title: What Alpaca Is and Is Not
docs.text:
• Alpaca 的 adaptation 是 SFT/instruction tuning，因为 LLaMA weights 被更新；
  • teacher model 负责生成 synthetic training data，但 student 在推理时不需要继续调用 teacher；
  • 它不是 ICL，因为 52K examples 用于训练，而不是全部塞入 prompt；
  • 它不是完整 RLHF，因为基本流程没有训练 reward model，也没有 PPO preference optimisation；
  • synthetic data 可以继承 teacher 的错误、bias 和输出风格，因此数据过滤很重要。

Claim: Alpaca distils instruction-following behaviour through generated demonstrations, not through an explicit reward model.

docs.title: Alpaca Exam Traps
docs.text:
• 把 175 seed tasks 当成最终全部训练数据；它们用于启动约 52K synthetic examples 的生成。
  • 认为 Alpaca 从零训练 7B 参数模型；它 fine-tunes pretrained LLaMA 7B。
  • 把 synthetic data generation 本身当作 RLHF。
  • 认为 teacher 和 student 必须有相同 architecture 或 tokenizer。
  • 认为生成数据天然正确；synthetic supervision 仍需要 filtering 和 evaluation。

docs.title: PEFT Motivation
docs.text:
PEFT (Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning)：冻结大部分 pretrained parameters，只训练少量参数或新增的小型组件。

Full fine-tuning: update all model parameters
PEFT:             freeze backbone + update small task-specific parameters
Prompting:        update no parameters

Full fine-tuning 在大模型上需要为全部参数保存 gradients 和 optimiser states，训练及每任务存储成本很高，还可能出现 overfitting、gradient interference 和 catastrophic forgetting。Prompting 无需训练，但会重复处理 prompt，受 context length、措辞和示例顺序影响，复杂任务上通常弱于 tuning。

Claim: PEFT aims to approach full fine-tuning performance while substantially reducing trainable parameters, memory, and per-task storage.

docs.title: Three PEFT Families
docs.text:
Family 改变什么 讲义代表方法 适用场景 主要代价 Parameter Composition 用 sparse/low-rank structure 表示参数或参数更新 pruning、sparse subnetworks、LoRA 可访问模型内部，希望用少量参数进行强适配 pruning 可能需反复 retraining；LoRA capacity 受 rank 限制 Input Composition 在输入或各层 attention context 中加入 learnable vectors prompt tuning、multi-layer prompt tuning backbone 必须 frozen，只训练 soft prompts 占用 context；较小模型和困难任务上表现较弱 Function Composition 在 frozen model 中插入或组合 task-specific functions adapters、IA3；LoRA 也可作为可切换 adapter 需要模块化切换或组合任务/领域能力 新模块增加 operations，可能有 inference overhead

Fast scenario test:

Train a low-rank change inside an open model      → Parameter Composition
Learn continuous vectors prepended to frozen LM  → Input Composition
Insert/switch small task modules in each layer   → Function Composition

docs.title: Parameter Composition: Pruning
docs.text:
Pruning：用 binary mask 删除模型中的部分 connections，形成 sparse subnetwork。

\[ W'=M\odot W,\qquad M_{ij}\in\{0,1\} \]

常见 magnitude pruning 删除绝对值最小的 weights：

Train → remove low-|w| connections → retrain remaining weights
  • One-shot pruning: 只执行一次 prune + retrain。
  • Iterative pruning: 多轮 prune + retrain，讲义指出更常见。
  • 优点：减少保留的 parameters/connections。
  • 局限：通常需要 retraining iterations；删除过多会损害 performance；非结构化 sparsity 不一定带来实际硬件加速。

docs.title: Parameter Composition: LoRA
docs.text:
LoRA (Low-Rank Adaptation)：冻结原始 weight matrix，只学习低秩的 task-specific weight update。

原始线性层：

\[ h=Wx \]

LoRA：

\[ \Delta W=BA,\qquad h=(W+\Delta W)x=Wx+BAx \]

其中：

\[ W\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}}\times d_{\text{in}}} \] \[ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{\text{in}}}, \qquad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}}\times r}, \qquad r\ll \min(d_{\text{in}},d_{\text{out}}) \]

训练时：

W: frozen
A, B: trainable

因此：

\[ \frac{\partial L}{\partial W}=0, \qquad \frac{\partial L}{\partial A},\frac{\partial L}{\partial B}\ne0 \]

Low-rank assumption: task adaptation 所需的有效 weight change 位于低维子空间，不必更新整个 full-rank matrix。

docs.title: LoRA Parameter Count
docs.text:
Full fine-tuning 一个 matrix 的参数量：

\[ d_{\text{out}}d_{\text{in}} \]

LoRA trainable parameters：

\[ r(d_{\text{in}}+d_{\text{out}}) \]

讲义例子：

W: 1024 × 1024      → 1,048,576 trainable parameters in full tuning
r = 8
A: 8 × 1024
B: 1024 × 8         → 16,384 trainable LoRA parameters
\[ 1-\frac{16{,}384}{1{,}048{,}576} =98.4375\% \]

即约减少 98.4% 的 trainable parameters。

docs.title: LoRA Training and Deployment
docs.text:
• 常将 A 随机初始化、B 初始化为 0，使训练开始时 \(BA=0\)，模型行为等于原 pretrained model。
  • 实际实现常使用 scaling：\(W'=W+\frac{\alpha}{r}BA\)。
  • LoRA 可加入 attention 的 \(W_Q,W_K,W_V,W_O\) 或 feedforward projections。
  • 每个任务只需保存小型 LoRA matrices，可共享同一个 frozen base model。
  • 部署时可合并：
\[ W_{\text{merged}}=W+BA \]

合并后仍是一个 dense matrix multiplication，因此不增加额外 inference latency。

QLoRA: 使用 quantised frozen base model（讲义示例为 4-bit）配合 trainable LoRA，以进一步降低显存。

讲义列出的其他 LoRA variants：

  • LoRA-FA: 在 LoRA 之外允许适配模型的更多部分，例如 biases 或 layer norms。
